shape_hint: Long hexagon nut: a hexagon prism three thread diameters long with a through thread, chamfered at both ends; side view is a rectangle of length l, end view a hexagon with width across flats s.
notes: Kept: width across flats s and length l (= 3 d) for M6-M36 - identical on fasteners.eu, globalfastener and fasten.it (schrauben-lexikon agrees for the sizes it lists). s for M10/M12/M14/M22 is 17/19/22/32 mm on all three (DIN 6334 keeps the old widths across flats; schrauben-lexikon prints '17, ISO 16' etc.). Pitch reaches three clusters only for M6, M8, M10, M12 (globalfastener, fastenerwholesale, lawsonproducts) and is left out so that all 12 sizes stay (2 columns x 12 sizes = 24 cells against 3 columns x 4 sizes = 12 cells). Independence caveat: fasteners.eu and globalfastener list the same 14 sizes and the same irregular 'e' series (29.56 for M18 and 35.03 for M22 next to 33.53 for M20 and 39.98 for M24), so they may share an origin. If a verifier merges them into one cluster, s and l still have 3 or more clusters (FE/GF, fasten.it, fastenerwholesale, lawsonproducts, schrauben-lexikon) for M6, M8, M10, M12, M16, M20, M24, M30, but only 2 for M14, M18, M22 and M36. Width across corners: fasteners.eu and globalfastener print a bare 'e' (11.05, 14.38, 18.9, 21.1, 24.49, 26.75, 29.56, 33.53, 35.03, 39.98, 50.85, 60.79), fasten.it prints 'e min' with 30.14 for M18 and 35.72 for M22; the numbers agree in 3 clusters for M6-M16, M20, M24, M30, M36 (see e_as_printed in coupling.evidence.json) but only one page says they are minimum values, so the candidate column e_min is not kept. boltport and torqbolt show a different 6-row table (not 3d) and nfgab's table mixes standard and non-standard items; neither is counted. keller-kalmbach product pages for DIN 6334 give no dimensions (probe saved as raw/kk_probe_din6334.html).

verification.checks_done: Verifier re-fetched every page itself on 2026-11-11 with curl (browser UA, 2.5 s pause per host; HTTP 200 for all; globalfastener detail_400 needed one retry after a 403), wrote its own stdlib HTML table reader (vt.py, gf.py, obs.py) and counting script (count.py) without using the researcher's raw/, extracted tables or scripts. Drawings that define bare symbols (schrauben-lexikon gifs, nfgab pngs) were fetched and viewed. Lead decisions applied: amesweb (calculator) not a source; a rival value printed by 2+ independent lineages removes the row; cells of another standard printed under the target title (verified equal to that standard's table) are neither support nor rival; pages reproducing the standard's text (boltport ISO 4035) excluded. A cluster whose own pages give two different values for a cell is not counted for it. Largest rectangle (cells, then rows) chosen among column subsets that contain the drawing keys. Re-counted 12 x 2 candidate cells; kept 8 x 2; per-cell clusters in coupling.verify.md.
